program: Integrated primary, dental and behavioral care
priceScope: Conditional whole annual unaudited recipient cost against partial dental health and signed household resources; not portfolio EV or marginal-gift price.

what: HHH provides integrated medical, dental, behavioral and supportive care for people affected by homelessness in Houston.
Services are free without an insurance requirement; transportation and partner delivery help patients reach care.
The initial assessment models a narrow dental channel, not depression treatment inferred from screening.
strengths: Defined federal dental counts and screening-versus-treatment distinction remain source checked.
Current free-service and transport mechanisms support explicit access and household resource assessment.
Annual clinical and signed resource components retain full negative costs and separate patient/household units.
reservations: Unaudited whole costs cover broad services; UDS and own dental visit scopes are unreconciled.
Utility, completion, local residence, household resources and net access costs remain judgments, not local causal effects.
Staffing, outside payer resources and gift-created capacity remain uncertain; donor HOLD persists.

sections.what: HHH provides integrated primary, dental, behavioral health and outreach care. Its 2025 annual report lists 6,433 people and 19,166 visits, while the federal UDS return lists 2,965 patients and 15,986 clinic visits plus 59 virtual visits under different, unreconciled reporting scopes. The UDS identifies 1,499 dental clinic visits and 595 dental patients. This partial model quantifies finite dental-pain relief only; other clinical benefits are unestimated, not assumed absent.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 UDS measure counts 659 patients screened for depression with follow-up documented as appropriate. That measure can include negative screens and does not establish 659 depressed people treated. Its separate remission cohort includes 55 eligible patients, with the outcome numerator suppressed; it is not a substitute denominator. The annual report lists 3,219 dental visits versus 1,499 UDS dental clinic visits, so completed symptomatic episodes and reporting scope require reconciliation. [Federal UDS workbook](https://data.hrsa.gov/DataDownload/StaticDocuments/H80-2025.xlsx) [Annual report](https://www.homeless-healthcare.org/s/FINAL-2025-Impact-Report.pdf)
sections.qualitative: Local integrated care plausibly meets substantial need, but visits do not prove incremental health gains. [Harris County file 26-5142](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=8167289&GUID=9F12FC50-645B-4A78-B668-6049CC4D835E&FullText=1), passed August 17, 2026, terminated a $70,000 dental project that HHH could not implement because of changing priorities and staffing challenges. The [original agreement](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/View.ashx?M=F&ID=15756863&GUID=E060471F-2059-41E2-8A54-E101BF76C76E) records no reimbursement as of May 31, 2026. This does not mean all dental care ceased; it does show that money alone did not resolve that project’s implementation constraint. The 2024 audit also raises liquidity and staffing-contract concerns. Patient clinical units are separate from resource household grouping. Current free services do not prove otherwise-paid medical cash savings; many people might otherwise forego care or use public alternatives. Resource central therefore uses zero cash and earnings as conservative unknown-coefficient judgments, with positive/negative alternatives; not evidence no resources improve. Screening remains screening, no depression QALY claim. Transportation, case management and job-training links do not establish jobs or net wages.
sections.cost: The full initial five-world report is frozen: central $55,628,242.40 health-only and historical signed scenario mixture $30,338,023.97, neither empirical EV. The revised conditional annual reference is $37,056,065.47 per better life: 2.3503667 clinical years plus −.2333567 signed household-resource equivalents. It removes the extra .6 gift-capacity discount from annual work and retains full .1 clinical harm, then adds explicit net resource costs; this is a boundary/accounting revision, not observed improved performance. Whole2025 unaudited expense $7,844,806 remains compared with narrow dental benefits. Estimated1499/3 episodes capped at595 reported patients are not measured completed symptomatic episodes. The .5 completion, .5 relief beyond alternatives, .08 utility and .25-year duration remain judgments. No observed dental-only cost allocation was found: .2 cost allocation sensitivity is explicitly hypothetical. Full and25% extra-resource cost cases remain. Other clinical and supportive portfolio effects are unknown, not zero.
sections.funding: Donor recommendation: HOLD. A city street-medicine agreement described a $700,000 two-year envelope with an initial term ending August 31, 2026; renewal is unverified. The separate $70,000 county dental project was terminated because HHH could not implement it, not because its gift gap was filled. The 2024 audit disclosed a $525,000 credit line due March 17, 2026; renewal and current liabilities are unverified. A current staffed care plan, grant restrictions and a priced incremental giving path are needed before recommending a gift. [City agreement](https://houston.novusagenda.com/agendapublic/CoverSheet.aspx?ItemID=35206&MeetingID=750) [County termination](https://harriscountytx.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=8167289&GUID=9F12FC50-645B-4A78-B668-6049CC4D835E&FullText=1) Signed resources use595patients × judged.8households, with judged.5incremental affordable-access share. Central otherwise-paid cash and net work gains are zero, $10net additional access/time/opportunity cost per exposedhousehold and$10,000baseline resources are judgments relative to alternative care; not patient fees (services are free), retail dental value or gross salary. Same household-year components are logged jointly with.5positive-overlap discount only; full negative costs remain even when completion or clinical relief fails. Positive work hypotheses additionally require clinical completion; no ordinary survivor earnings. Cash receipt is independent of clinical symptom response. Extra outside payer loss for local transfers is globally included once in disjoint-cohort stresses. Central zero external loss is donor-budget accounting convention, not proof partner/public costs absent; costs already in recipient budget are not added twice. Clinical-null/financial-only/unknown/adverse and no-exposure cases retain the relevant signed distinctions. Gift-created staffing capacity remains separate unknown.

model.costScope: Whole 2025 unaudited organizational expense divided by a narrower UDS dental-only benefit pathway. Historical exploratory whole-cost/partial-benefit proxy, not current marginal gift price. Annual report 3219 dental visits versus UDS1499 remains unresolved; UDS selected as the narrower clearly defined series. Cross-pathway overlap multiplier removed because there is only one quantified benefit pathway.
model.geographicAttribution: Care sites and patient ZIP rows support local delivery, but 449 of 2,965 UDS patients are grouped as Other ZIP Codes and some small cells are suppressed. The modeled 95–100% Houston-metro benefit share is a judgment, not measured residence.
model.formula: Clinical = (min(dentalPatients,visits/visitsPerEpisode)*completion*additionalRelief*utility*finiteYears - full exposed harm)*localShare. Resource households = dentalPatients*unique; incremental cash access distinct from clinical response; positive work requires completion. Joint same-year net flows use shared .5log income bridge, full negative burdens and distinct payer loss once. Annual work excludes separate gift-response multiplier.
model.counterfactual: Harris Health/public, insured and other providers or foregone care can substitute. Cash savings require actual otherwise-paid consumption after alternatives, not retail service value. Net time costs are additional relative to that alternative; existing gift-funded capacity and renewal uncertain separately.
model.attribution: Dental care alone quantified; visit-derived episodes capped by observed patient envelope. Clinical patients never household-deduplicated. Clinical completion and alternatives remain judgments. Annual denominator does not use extra marginal-gift capacity multiplier; staffing expansion unknown separately.
model.uncertainty: Very low confidence, partial-health model. UDS/annual-report activity scopes are unreconciled. Scenario weights are subjective, not calibrated probabilities; the favorable case drives most weighted positive benefit. Marginal gift impact and staffing response are unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: UDS dental clinic visits divided by assumed visits per symptomatic episode, then assumed completion, incremental relief, finite utility and duration; not observed cured patients.
